questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: Relativistic momentum against velocity
questions.learningObjective: Identify how relativistic momentum responds to speed near light speed.
questions.stem: The lead designer wants a momentum chart for a spacecraft bus that will coast for decades and asks how momentum responds to speed near light speed.

options.text: Momentum grows faster than speed once the craft speed is a large fraction of light speed
Momentum stays proportional to speed all the way up to the speed of light itself
options.misconception: assumes the Newtonian relation survives at relativistic speed

options.text: Momentum levels off at a fixed ceiling once the craft is moving quickly
options.misconception: believes relativistic momentum saturates at a finite limit

options.text: Momentum depends only on the mass of the bus and ignores how fast it travels
options.misconception: treats momentum as mass only, ignoring the velocity term

questions.explanation: Relativistic momentum is p equals gamma times m times v, so it climbs steeply at high speed. A ceiling applies to speed, not to momentum, which grows without bound as the craft nears light speed.
questions.hint: Write p as gamma times m times v and let gamma grow.

questions.topic: The classical limit of the total energy
questions.learningObjective: Explain why the relativistic total energy exceeds the classical estimate.
questions.stem: A test cell plots measured total energy against the classical estimate for a fast probe and finds a clear excess that widens with speed.

options.text: The excess is sensor drift, since the classical formula already accounts for all energy
options.misconception: dismisses the excess as instrument error, not physics

options.text: The excess grows as the speed rises because the Lorentz factor multiplies the rest energy
The excess is constant because the rest energy term dominates at every speed
options.misconception: believes the excess stays fixed at all speeds of the probe

options.text: The excess appears only above light speed, which the probe has already exceeded
options.misconception: assumes relativistic effects need speeds beyond light speed

questions.explanation: Total energy is E equals gamma times m c squared, and gamma grows as speed rises, so the excess over the classical value widens. Relativity produces this at any speed, not only near light speed.
questions.hint: Compare E equals gamma m c squared with m c squared.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.topic: What converting a mass into energy releases
questions.learningObjective: Explain why converting rest mass to heat releases an enormous amount of energy.
questions.stem: During a shutdown test the fuel plant converts a stored rest mass into heat and asks why the released energy is so enormous.

answer.exemplar: The rest mass of the fuel is already a store of energy, because mass and energy are two forms of the same quantity. Converting that mass into heat releases m c squared joules for every kilogram involved, roughly nine times ten to the sixteen joules per kilogram, far more than any chemical reaction can deliver.

questions.explanation: Mass is a form of energy, so destroying the rest structure releases E equals m c squared, around nine times ten to the sixteen joules per kilogram. Burning fuel merely rearranges molecules and releases a tiny share.
questions.hint: Mass itself converts to energy at m c squared per kilogram.

answer.exemplar: Chemical burning and mass conversion release energy from different mechanisms. Mass conversion destroys the rest structure instead, so the entire rest mass, or nearly all of it, is released as energy at m c squared joules per kilogram, which is why even a partial conversion dwarfs any chemical reaction.

questions.explanation: Burning releases only the small mass defect between reactants and products, while mass conversion releases the rest mass itself at m c squared per kilogram. Even converting a fraction of the mass therefore dwarfs any chemical release.
